PAST-MISTAKES-LIBRARY.md.to:
## A link to paid modding content went onto 33 Nexus pages before anyone read Nexus's anti-solicitation policy (2026-10-02)

**What happened.** Asked to add a link to every mod page, Claude added it to all 58 distro pages and all 33 live pages, verified every one - and checked nothing about whether Nexus allows it. The owner then asked for the policy to be checked. Nexus allows donation links but its Anti-Solicitation Policy forbids offering files, updates or modding-related services in exchange for money. The line came out again the same day.

**Why it looked fine.** The owner had asked for it, and the page already carried a donation link - the difference between a donation link and a link to paid modding content was not looked for.

**Do instead.** Before putting anything on a public page that points at money, read the platform's own policy for that kind of link and say what it allows before posting.

rules/03-versioning-and-release.md.to:
## 35. A bug report has to reach the mod's author by a route that is watched

Reports arrive on each mod's own Bugs and Posts tabs, not only on one dedicated page. The original kept a single "request hub" page with tagged submissions and a scheduled poller. Relying on it silently cost real reports: the hub page was removed by Nexus staff for not being a mod, and the poller read the placeholder that a removed page still serves as "nothing new".

- A route that is checked by a tool needs a check on the tool: zero entries from a page that had entries is a failure, not a quiet day.
- Watch the pages the reports actually arrive on, the mods' own, and read them directly whenever the queue may be stale.
- A tag on a submission's first line saves guessing its category; an untagged one still goes on the to-do list instead of being dropped.
- The poller reaches the internet, so it is not in the kit (`OPTIONAL-SCRIPTS.md`, item 8).
